newsitem.title: USA: Casino trip bus hijacked, driver shot in face.
newsitem.headline: Casino trip bus hijacked, driver shot in face.

text.p: Three men hijacked a bus taking elderly Texans to gamble in Louisiana and shot the driver in the face, but they were captured after a passenger alerted police on her cellular phone, police said Friday.

The bus, carrying 60 people from Dallas to the Louisiana casino town of Bossier City, was hijacked Thursday night near the east Texas town of Tyler. Three men jumped up from their seats, pulled out guns and began robbing the passengers.
"Their intention was to rob everybody, take the jewelry and money and escape with their partner who was probably already following the bus in another car," Smith County Sheriff J.B. Smith said.
But one woman slipped lower in her seat and quietly called on a cell phone to police, who caught up to the bus and forced it to pull over on a major highway.

The hijackers, angry when the driver stopped the bus, shot him in the face and ran into nearby woods. They were captured as police, some on horseback, used dogs to track them down. Police later also arrested the gunmen's accomplice, who had been following behind the bus in a getaway car.
Hospital officials in Tyler, about 90 miles (135 km) southeast of Dallas, said the driver, Michael Gibbs, was in critical condition but was expected to survive.
The bus passengers, most of whom were elderly, were returned to Dallas Friday morning.
"The bus driver really saved us. He told them 'Just go ahead and shoot me but I'm gonna stop,'" one man told reporters.
